summary: ph-common exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at install and require time
details: ph-common@0.1.0 ships a beacon.cjs that collects hostname, install path, current working directory, and node version and POSTs them to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The beacon runs via the package's postinstall hook (node beacon.cjs) and is also invoked at the top of index.js (the declared main) inside a try/catch, so `require('ph-common')` triggers the same outbound call. The module then exports a no-op Proxy stub so consumers don't error, meaning the package has no functional library surface — its only effect is to transmit installer workspace identifiers to the hardcoded IP. The install path and cwd fields disclose non-public developer/project directory information to an operator who controls the bare-IP endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
